title: Smoothing with moving means
log: 2026-11-02T04:35:41Z autoreview: cleared with the fix (card wording)

draft.title: Smoothing with moving means
card: Smoothing replaces each value in a time series with the mean of it and the values next to it. This evens out short-term ups and downs so the overall pattern is easier to see.
For a 3-point moving mean, average a value with the one before and the one after. Example: for 10, 14, 12, the smoothed middle value is (10 + 14 + 12) ÷ 3 = 12.
An odd-point mean (3 or 5) is centred on a real data point. The first and last values have no full set of neighbours, so they get no smoothed value.
An even-point mean, such as 4-point, falls halfway between two time points. Centre it by averaging two neighbouring 4-point means. The result lines up with a real time point.
draft.remember: Average each value with its neighbours. Even-point means need a second averaging to centre them.

a.q: A 3-point moving mean is used on the values 8, 11, 17, 14. What is the smoothed value for the second point?
a.why: The second point is averaged with its neighbours: (8 + 11 + 17) ÷ 3 = 36 ÷ 3 = 12. Answering 11 just keeps the original value and does no smoothing.
a.clue: Add the second value and the two beside it, then divide by 3.

b.q: Sales at a kiosk in Ballarat are 20, 26, 22, 28, 30 in five time periods. A 4-point moving mean gives 24 (between periods 2 and 3) and 26.5 (between periods 3 and 4). What is the centred 4-point mean for period 3?
b.why: Centre it by averaging the two 4-point means: (24 + 26.5) ÷ 2 = 25.25. Giving 50.5 forgets to divide by 2 after adding.
b.clue: Average the two means that sit either side of period 3.

problems.detail: The card names 3- and 5-point means together, then says only 'the first and last values' get no smoothed value. For a 5-point mean, the first two and last two values get none, so students could misapply this.

check.summary: Both questions and their explanations are correct. One small card issue: the note about end values gets no smoothed value is only true for a 3-point mean, not a 5-point mean, as the card implies.
